In [[rocket]]ry, the '''Goddard problem''' is to optimize the peak [[altitude]] of a rocket, ascending vertically, and taking into account [[atmospheric drag]] and the [[gravitational field]]. This was first posed by [[Robert H. Goddard]] in his 1919 publication, "A Method of Reaching Extreme Altitudes".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dept.aoe.vt.edu/~cliff/aoe5244_99/week_13_a.pdf |title=Goddard Problem (slides) |author= E.M. Cliff |access-date=2010-04-29 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100624035050/http://www.aoe.vt.edu/~cliff/aoe5244_99/week_13_a.pdf |archive-date=2010-06-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite report |url= https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/citations/AD0409855 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20210927132400/https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/citations/AD0409855 |url-status= live |archive-date= September 27, 2021 |title=A Solution of the Goddard Problem |author= Boris Garfinkel}}</ref>
